answer: A stone chapel choir gives each singer one vertex of the loft, a velvet stole with a numbered clasp. Each morning the choirmaster sings a call and each singer answers with the echo in their own voice, holding the note till it fades, and the choirmaster writes the match in the choir book. A second choirmaster hears the call at dusk and strikes any voice whose echo drifts or whose stole never left its peg. A thousand fake names need a thousand trained voices and a thousand answered echoes, and one forger cannot sing a thousand parts in a single morning.
